messages:
simon: Heads-up — after the fused-attn merge yesterday I'm seeing a 15-25% throughput drop for long-context work (seq_len >= 1024) when KV cache is enabled. tokens/sec down, $/M tokens up. Not universal (shorter seqs fine).

kevin: Oof. Can you paste the quick numbers? which model / batch sizes?

simon: Quick snapshot from perf harness (gpt2-like, fp16, A100):
```
# kernel, seq, batch, tokens/sec, $/M_tokens
flashattention-v1, 512, 8, 120000, $8.3
fused-attn-optimized, 512, 8, 118000, $8.5
flashattention-v1, 1024, 4, 72000, $13.8
fused-attn-optimized, 1024, 4, 56000, $17.7  <-- regression
paged-attn, 1024, 4, 74000, $13.4
```
(Those numbers are median across 6 runs)

maria: That's interesting — paged-attn beats fused for long seq with small batch. Any KV cache differences?

simon: Yes: regression only when KV cache ON. With cold-start (no cache) fused-attn is fine. With persistent KV the fused kernel appears to re-copy kv tensors every generation step for seq>=1024.

anya: Can you point at the commit? I can bisect if we have a narrow window.

simon: PR was merged: commit abc1234 (runtime: fused-attn improvements). I ran a quick bisect and the change in allocator flags + a refactor in kernel selection seems correlated.

kevin: Possible hypotheses: 1) fused kernel expects contiguous pinned buffers and our KV layout changed so we do an extra memcpy to pinned pages; 2) tiled perf path changed cache eviction heuristics.

maria: I captured a short nvprof trace. Copying the most relevant lines: 
```
Memcpy HtoD  8.3ms  size=~12MB  (hot path after each token)
kernel fused_attn_launch 1.6ms
kernel flash_attn_launch 0.9ms
```
Shows extra host->device copies when KV cache is on with fused.

perf-bot: Artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/1765204821/fused-kv-copy-trace

kevin: Run with forced kernel selector and mem flags to confirm:
```
export RW_ATTENTION_KERNEL=PREFER:flash,paged,fused
export RW_FORCE_PINNED=true
python perf/run_attention_bench.py --model gpt2 --seq 1024 --batch 4 --kv-cache true --runs 6
```
If forcing flash/paged restores throughput then selector change is the culprit.

simon: Quick experiments: forcing flash brings tokens/sec back to ~72k. forcing fused keeps it low. Forcing pinned allocator reduced memcpy but didn't fully recover.

anya: Sounds like fused kernel path still triggers an extra staging buffer for KV layout conversions. Can you dump the buffer shapes / strides right before the kernel launch? small snippet to add to runtime: 
```
log.debug("kv layout pre-launch", shape=kv.shape, stride=kv.stride, dtype=kv.dtype, device=kv.device)
```

maria: I'll add that and re-run for seq 512/1024 with kv-on/off. Also logging tflops-per-kernel and memcpy times.

kevin: Also let's add a quick perf regression alert: if tokens/sec drops >10% for canonical workload (gpt2, seq=1024, batch=4, kv=on) mark PR as blocking.

simon: Agreement. I'll open a short incident and tag the fused-attn PR for revert if bisect pins it.

anya: FYI — paging/pinned interplay was tweaked in 2025-12-08 commit def567. Could be related.

maria: Re-run queued, will post numbers in ~30m.

perf-bot: Reminder: please attach raw traces + env (CUDA, driver, libcudnn) when posting results.

kevin: Thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the trace analysis ping me. :eyes:
